Three types of files that are discussed: processor, program, and data files.
Processor files are files sent to the PLC via an RS-232 Serial Port. A processor file contains both program and data files..
Processor files contain user instructions, data, configurations, and can be transferred from a computer to a PLC or vice versa.
Some PLC systems use modems to communicate with distant PLC's.
Program files contain three program types: the system program, main ladder program, and the subroutine ladder program. These three programs are required for every processor file.
You can have anywhere from 3 to 255 program files. File 0 is reserved for the system program; files 1 and 2 are for the main ladder program; and files 3 through 255 are for the subroutine programs..
The system program contains I/O configuration, the processor type and name, and other system oriented information.
The main ladder program contains user program instructions that tell the processor how to operate.
Subroutine ladder programs are short segments of program code that can be retrieved (called) from the parent program for the purpose of performing repetitive operations.
Data files contain information used by the main and subroutine ladder programs. As with the program files, certain data files have pre-defined types.
0 - output data 3 - bit data 6 - control data
1 - input data 4 - timer data 7 - integer data
2 - status data 5 - counter data 8 - system dataaaaaaaaaaaa
The pre-defined types are the first 9 files: 0 - output data 3 - bit data 6 - control data 1 - input data 4 - timer data 7 - integer data 2 - status data 5 - counter data 8 - system dataaaaaa
Files 9 - 255 are user-defined files and contain information needed by the program. These files must be of a type listed in the first eight (0 through 7).

Before you learn how to transfer programs to the PLC, it is important to understand the communications link and the PLC's modes of operation. The PLC must be linked to the computer and in the proper mode for proper operation.
The communications link must be established prior to monitoring or transferring data between the computer and the SLC-500 PLC.
There are several processor modes for the SLC-500 PLC. We will discuss two of these modes: off-line and remote run.
In the program mode, processor files can be transferred to/from the PLC from the computer. In this mode, no program execution is performed.
In run mode, ladder programs are executed and their output can be monitored. It is important to note that ladder program files cannot be modified while in run mode.
In run mode, however, you can modify the processor data files, which is very helpful when fine-tuning a ladder program. You can also transfer a processor file from the PLC to the computer.
Let's see how to change the processor's mode. First we will establish a communications link between the computer and the PLC.
If the processor isn't connected properly and the communications link program is not running, the RSLogix software will not be able to communicate with the PLC.
Communication is necessary to transfer information to and from the PLC processor. We will simulate the communication.
When communicating between the computer and the PLC, power must be applied to the PLC. For purposes of our simulation, we will stipulate that power has been applied to the PLC..

1. The two important modes of operation are: program mode and run mode.
2. In the program mode, files can be transferred to and from the PLC, and both data and program files can be modified.
3. In run mode, evaluation of the processor file in the PLC memory begins immediately. Data files can be modified in this mode, but not program files.

To transfer the project files to/from the PLC, the download or upload modes are used.
In download mode, processor files are transferred to the PLC from the computer. In this mode, no program execution is being performed.
In upload mode, processor files are transferred from the PLC to the computer. In this mode, no program execution is being performed.
